analysis: Both changed files (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) are documentation only. The PR adds repository-ownership guidance: centralized coordinator/backend code belongs in Layr-Labs/darkbloom-platform, not d-inference. It also adds sibling-clone setup instructions, notes that the retained coordinator/console directories are transitional copies, and says protocol changes are to be split by owning repository. No executable code, configuration, deployment, trust-boundary, attestation, encryption, authorization, billing or data-flow behavior changes. AGENTS.md (lines 3, 7-43, 47-48) states hop-by-hop encryption, with the coordinator decrypting inside its confidential VM and the provider as the plaintext endpoint. That is consistent with T-003 and A-001 and does not contradict the canonical model. AGENTS.md line 14 and CONTRIBUTING.md lines 17-25 explicitly do not authorize deleting source, changing hosting or deploying; production deploys still require human approval (AGENTS.md lines 285-288). Possible later review concern: coordinator code remains in this repository, and the threat model's affected_files (for example T-049's coordinator/mediafetch paths) still cite those paths. A future move of the code to darkbloom-platform would need threat-model file references and the CI/security tests re-anchored, but this PR does not move anything. CONTRIBUTING.md line 163 still points protocol sync at coordinator/protocol/messages.go, and CONTRIBUTING.md lines 159-161 explain the split. No finding was filed. Coverage limit: only these docs were examined; no code or callers were supplied.
